cs.t:
I have 4 Coway and 2 Winix purifiers and I can confirm: they're great sleep noise generators! The plastic front pieces and the filters themselves block/baffle any high frequency noise from the fans, leaving you with a pleasant low/mid frequency  whooooooosh.  I like it better than the sound from small cheap solid state machines; their small speakers can't do low frequencies.       For most circumstances where someone would use 
    a white noise machine, this kind of small purifier 
    is all-around better. 
  
Hmm. The word "most" is doing a lot of work here. Depends if you enjoy fresh air when you sleep or not. If you've ever monitored CO2 levels you know how quickly they climb in a closed room. But, if you are blowing fresh air into a room, or have the windows open, the filtration effectiveness of these units approaches zero pretty rapidly. And these air purifiers aren't exactly free to run: they use ~50-100W of power and if you run them 24/7 you can expect to spend $100+ per year on filters. So there's no perfect answer...

cs.t: I have a Winix air purifier from Costco in my bedroom, and it has a small air quality indicator light (blue -> yellow -> red) though I'm too lazy to look up what it's measuring. Surprisingly, making the bed, shaking out the sheets, or vacuuming doesn't make it change color. But farting in the room makes it red for minutes. An ever amusing phenomenon that makes my girlfriend and I chuckle on a weekly basis.
cs.th: Frying Eggs and Air Quality Tests

cs.t: Winix air quality sensors (at least the ones I have) measure volatile organic compounds (VOCs), which is a little ironic since HEPA purifiers do little to remove VOCs from the air. Some other air purifiers like Coways measure particle pollution.
